description: Supplier shipment is late; inbound stock and customer commitments are exposed.
Available stock is below committed order demand; evaluate transfers and split fulfilment.
Route closure adds transit time; identify shipments and orders on affected corridor.
Inbound shipment is held for documentation; identify downstream stock risk.
A batch is quarantined after inspection; held stock must not be allocated.
Demand rises sharply for fast-moving SKUs; forecast stockout and protect priority orders.
Warehouse capacity drops; reroute inbound shipments and rebalance fulfilment.
Severe weather affects regional hubs; revise ETAs and reprioritise impacted orders.
Fuel prices rise sharply, increasing carrier quotes and making some expedited recovery plans uneconomic.
Congestion at a major port increases dwell time for multiple inbound shipments and threatens replenishment dates.
A key supplier temporarily stops production, affecting multiple open purchase orders and dependent customer orders.
A temperature-sensitive shipment exceeds its permitted range and is held pending quality disposition; unsafe stock cannot be allocated.
